entry noun

the way in, an entrance (the place)

also entrance, the entrance, entryway, doorway, at the entrance

classical

Caes. B.G. 5.9: omnēs introitūs erant praeclūsī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Caecin. 8: ad omnēs introitūs, quā adīrī poterat (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 310

introitus, introitūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an entrance, a way in

The place where one goes in, of a building, a harbour (Caes. B.C. 3.39) or a wood; also the going in itself (see entry, the going in).

Other words

  • aditus, aditūs m. — an approach, an entrance

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 5.9.1: angustō in aditū; Caes. B.G. 4.20; Liv. 36.10 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 310 · Declension on Wiktionary

    The way one approaches a place, and so its entrance; also the chance of approaching a person (see access).

  • ōstium, ōstiī n. — doorway, entrance

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 310 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • angustō in aditū taurus luctāns cornibus cum vix intrāre posset ad praesēpia, mōnstrābat vitulus quō sē pactō plecteret

    when a bull, struggling with his horns in a narrow entrance, could hardly get in to his stall, a calf showed him how to twist himselfPhaedr. 5.9.1–3

  • omnēs introitūs erant praeclūsī

    every entrance had been blockedCaes. B.G. 5.9 (Lewis & Short)

See also entry, access, door, front door, hall, enter.
